 U.Va. Health acquires $37.7 million, 55-acre facility to increase outpatient care 
 The Board of Visitors also approved housing and dining rates for the 2027-28 academic year during its Friday afternoon meeting
 Board of Visitors meeting, photographed Oct. 30, 2026.
 Photo by Mac Doucette 
 | The Cavalier Daily
 By Edward Christopher 
 October 30, 2026 
 Estimated reading time: 3 minutes 
 The full Board of Visitors convened Friday to hear about the acquisition of a site to expand outpatient care from University President Scott Beardsley and Dr. Mitchell Rosner, chief executive officer of U.Va. Health and executive vice president for health affairs. U.Va. Health plans to have the first patients treated in the building by 2028, Rosner noted. The Board also approved 2027-28 academic year housing and dining rates for the University and College at Wise. 
 The acquisition is a 55-acre and 365,000-square-foot building in the Pantops area of Albemarle County, which was formerly home to a State Farm operations center. U.Va. Health purchased the property for $48.3 million, but received a payment from the previous tenant for early termination of lease obligation, reducing the net purchase price to $37.7 million. The acquired property, located at 1500 State Farm Blvd., is near U.S. 250 and Interstate 64. 
 Beardsley said that U.Va. Health’s demand for patient care is on the rise, both for inpatient and outpatient care. For inpatient care, patients stay at least one night in a facility, and for outpatient care, patients are not admitted overnight — these visits are typically for check-ups, treatments and tests. Beardsley said that by 2035, U.Va. Health predicts that 1.2 million outpatient visits will take place in Charlottesville annually, which is 300,000 more than the current number of annual outpatient visits.
 According to Beardsley, the acquisition will also revitalize the area. He said the office has been vacant since Statefarm stopped using the facility in 2020, when it moved employees to remote work. He also said that the property will have outdoor walking paths for doctors, staff and patients. 
 “The acquisition of this property is an investment in the health of our communities that we serve every day,” Beardelsy said. “That provides a giant step forward for our mission of patient care and public service.” 
 Rosner said that the next six months will be spent developing a master plan for the space, including through establishing what outpatient services are relocated to this area and where renovations are needed. He said that these decisions will involve clinical leaders, physicians and care teams. By relocating some outpatient services to the Pantops property, Rosner said University hospital space is made available for inpatient care.
 “We can create a more convenient experience for patients, and importantly, reduce the congestion on the main medical campus,” Rosner said. “This is especially important as we think about serving more patients who need specialized care, including those referred to us from other hospitals throughout the Commonwealth.”
 In addition to the announcement of the new outpatient center, Jennifer Wagner Davis, University executive vice president and chief operating officer, delivered a presentation to the Board on proposed dining and housing rates for the 2027-28 academic year, which were unanimously approved by Board members following the presentation. 
 Davis said that rates are normally brought to the Board at its regular December meeting of each year. However, because of increased housing opportunities in the private sector and requests from students regarding information for housing on the Ivy Emmet Corridor, such as pricing, Davis said she wants to begin advertising on-Grounds housing. 
 Several new luxury apartment buildings are currently under construction off Grounds, including VERVE Charlottesville, Blume on Ivy and The Adelaide . All three will be open for student residents for the 2027-28 academic year. 
 Approvals for the University’s 2027-28 academic year housing and dining rates include an average double room rate increase of $441 — or 4.8 percent — according to Wagner’s presentation. This increases the average double room cost from $8,748 for the current academic year to $9,189 for the 2027-28 academic year. 
 Additionally, Davis said there are 8,250 beds on Grounds and about 44 percent of undergraduate students live on Grounds. She also noted that the double room rate of $8,748 for the current academic year is $1,700 cheaper compared to “peer” institutions. 
 According to the presentation, the increases for meal plan rates are between $160 and $360, as the Board approved an average increase of $241, or 4.99 percent for the 2027-28 academic year during the Friday meeting. Current meal plan rates are between $2,120 and $7,340 per year — students can choose from a variety of plans that differ in cost, from an all access plan that provides unlimited meals each semester to a Block 50 plan that provides 50 meals per semester. The approved rates for the 2027-28 academic year are between $1,320 and $7,700, depending on the meal plan a student chooses. Compared to “peer” institutions, Davis said that current University dining plans are $660 cheaper per year. 
 Jackson Sleadd, student representative to the Board and fourth-year College student, supported approving on-Grounds housing rates to allow students and families to better understand the housing market as they begin signing leases for the next academic year. He requested that in the future, approval of annual rates take place at the September Board meeting.  
 “I remember last year the scramble to find a lease in late August,” Sleadd said. “Talking to my friends over the summer and early in September about where we were going to live the next year [was] very stressful. Approving the rates now allows students and their families to get a better sense of what the market will actually look like.”
 Edward Christopher Edward Christopher is a staff writer on the news desk as well as a member of the advertising team for The Cavalier Daily. He is a second-year Commerce student from Northern Virginia. Edward enjoys covering state politics and University developments.
